questions.question: Set the trailer air supply control to "emergency" position to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before every trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then test the emergency brakes by pulling out the trailer air supply control. Drive forward slowly with the tractor. The trailer should not move if the brakes work correctly.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before every trip, inspect all couplings. There must be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, the best action is to:

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel left and right.

questions.explanation: If your trailer skids, release the brakes to regain traction. The trailer will straighten out once the wheels grip the road again.

questions.question: To check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Check for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: For vehicles built before 1998, check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes. This tells you if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: Shut-off valves:

options.text: Prevent air from leaving air brake systems.
Prevent air from entering air brake systems.
Override vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent air from leaving air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers in air supply lines. The rear shut-off valve must always be closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, position the trailer slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, make sure the:
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to make sure air reaches all brakes on all trailers. Listen for air escaping to confirm. Then close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: To test ____, apply your brakes with the hand control while moving the vehicle forward slowly.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, first check that air pressure is normal. Release the parking brake and move forward slowly. Use the hand control to apply the brakes. If the brakes work, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: You take a turn too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: You take a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To prevent rollovers, drive slowly on ramps and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when towing trailers.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking during hard braking. When ABS detects wheels about to lock, it reduces braking pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, what will happen?
questions.explanation: When a trailer skids, release the brakes to help the tires grip the road again. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to tip over if a driver turns too quickly?
questions.explanation: When turning, steer slowly and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver should:

options.text: Not apply the trailer hand brake.
Use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: When a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake. Braking is what caused the wheels to lock in the first place.

questions.question: If you must cross traffic while driving a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for you.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
Use only your mirrors to check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, wait for a large enough gap to cross safely.

questions.question: Trailers with low ground clearance are difficult to drive over:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are hard to cross with a trailer that has low ground clearance. Long trailers with single-axle tractors are especially difficult to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that drives faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Bobtail tractors are hard to operate and require caution.

questions.question: How should you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply fill up, turning off the engine, and then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure gets too low.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle with stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully loaded one. With less weight, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have less traction.

questions.question: Before beginning a trip, you should:

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to let air reach all trailers. Listen for escaping air. Then close both valves before you drive.
